name: Vibe Kanban
vendor: BloopAI (bloop, shut down 2026-04-10; project continues community maintained)

surfaces.label: Vibe Kanban desktop app (Tauri v2). The axum server runs INSIDE this process (server::startup::start in crates/tauri-app/src/main.rs), so this one pid holds every workspace and every agent child. Bundle id is tauri.conf.json `identifier`. Installed by `npx vibe-kanban --desktop` into /Applications, then ~/Applications, then the cache dir (npx-cli/src/desktop.ts), or from the GitHub release dmg `Vibe.Kanban_<ver>_aarch64.dmg`. Bundle folder is `Vibe Kanban.app` (bundleName). Main executable name is INFERRED: Tauri defaults to the cargo binary, `vibe-kanban-tauri`; matched on the .app folder as well as the name so either is caught. WebKit helpers are separate system processes and do not match. A host: report the app pid only; a session state needs the SQLite or HTTP read in working_signals.

Browser-mode server: the Rust binary `vibe-kanban` that `npx vibe-kanban` downloads (zip from the vendor R2 bucket) and unpacks to ~/.vibe-kanban/bin/<tag>/macos-arm64/vibe-kanban, then runs with execSync(`"<bin>"`) (npx-cli/src/cli.ts extractAndRun). It serves the web UI on 127.0.0.1:<auto port> (HOST and PORT/BACKEND_PORT override) and opens a browser. Matched by exact executable name, NOT by path: the same folder also holds `vibe-kanban-mcp` (a stdio MCP server that agents launch, not a session) and `vibe-kanban-review`, and path_contains is a substring test that would catch both. The node launcher (`node .../bin/cli.js`, argv[0] is `node`) is deliberately not matched: it is only a parent, and the probe keeps the outermost match, which would hide the server. One server holds every workspace, so this is a host.

session_store.note: No per_session path: a host process cannot be mapped to one file by an argument, and the session id is a VK uuid that never appears on any command line. Two stores under the data dir ~/Library/Application Support/ai.bloop.vibe-kanban (directories::ProjectDirs("ai","bloop","vibe-kanban"), utils/src/assets.rs): (1) sessions/<first 2 chars of session uuid>/<session uuid>/processes/<execution process uuid>.jsonl, one file per execution process (one agent turn, or one setup/cleanup/dev script), one serialised LogMsg per line (Stdout, Stderr, JsonPatch, SessionId, MessageId, Ready, Finished); older runs kept the same lines in the execution_process_logs table (logs TEXT, JSONL). (2) db.v2.sqlite, journal_mode DELETE (no WAL): tables workspaces (container_ref, branch, archived), sessions (id, workspace_id, executor, name), execution_processes (session_id, run_reason, status, exit_code, started_at, completed_at), coding_agent_turns (execution_process_id, agent_session_id, prompt, summary, seen). Read status columns only: prompt, summary and the log lines are private conversation. config.json, profiles.json, credentials.json sit beside them. The agent's OWN transcript (for example ~/.claude/projects) is written by the npx-launched agent as usual and is what `--resume <agent_session_id>` in the follow-up command line points at. Worktrees are separate: $TMPDIR/vibe-kanban/worktrees/<workspace dir>/<repo name> (or <custom root>/.vibe-kanban-workspaces/), and that is each agent child's cwd. Release builds only: debug builds use <repo>/dev_assets and $TMPDIR/vibe-kanban-dev.

working_signals.name: ~/Library/Application Support/ai.bloop.vibe-kanban/db.v2.sqlite
working_signals.meaning: Exact truth is SQL, and the probe cannot run it (no sqlite signal, no per_session path): SELECT s.workspace_id, ep.session_id FROM execution_processes ep JOIN sessions s ON s.id = ep.session_id WHERE ep.status = 'running' AND ep.run_reason = 'codingagent' AND ep.dropped = 0. One coding-agent execution process is one turn (an initial prompt or one follow-up; each follow-up spawns a NEW process), it is inserted 'running' when the agent child is spawned and set completed, failed or killed when it exits (crates/db/src/models/execution_process.rs, crates/executors/src/executors/claude.rs spawn_follow_up). Do NOT use the app's own `is_running` flag or run_reason IN ('setupscript','cleanupscript'): those also count setup and cleanup scripts. Guards: a row stays 'running' after a crash until the next server start rewrites it to failed (cleanup_orphan_executions), so require the server pid alive; the row stays 'running' while a turn waits on a tool approval. As a bare mtime the file only says something committed: it is one shared file, rolled by any workspace, archive or pin change, so it can raise working for a project with one live server but never lower it. Same answer over HTTP without opening the file: POST /api/workspaces/summaries {"archived":false} on the local port returns latest_process_status ('running'), has_pending_approval and latest_session_id per workspace (crates/server/src/routes/workspaces/workspace_summary.rs); note its latest process may also be a setup or cleanup script. Not observed: VK is not installed here.

working_signals.name: ~/Library/Application Support/ai.bloop.vibe-kanban/sessions/*/*/processes/*.jsonl
working_signals.meaning: The per-execution-process raw log, appended line by line as the agent streams (spawn_stream_raw_logs_to_storage in crates/services/src/services/execution_process.rs). A write in the last 30 s raises working; quiet does not prove idle (a long tool call or model call is silent), and a script or dev-server process writes here too, so it cannot tell an agent turn from `npm run dev`. Unobserved.

Weak, inferred and uncalibrated. Floor 10 follows registry/README.md section 4 (desktop hosts and hosts holding dev servers use 10, not the 5 guessed earlier). The tree holds every agent (npx -> sh -> node or native agent, all doing model I/O with little CPU) but also dev-server scripts and terminal panes that the user starts from Vibe Kanban, which burn CPU for hours with no agent turn. Never the only reason. child_process and tool_children are deliberately absent: (a) agent children are usually `node` (npx is a node script, so argv[0] is `node`), (b) a dev-server script `zsh -c 'npm run dev'` exec's in place and shows up as a direct child `node` for its whole life, (c) PTY terminals are permanent direct shell children, (d) executor option discovery spawns short agent children at server start and on each use (executors/utils.rs spawn_global_cache_refresh_for_agent; OpenCode spawns a server).

waiting_signals.endpoint: ws://127.0.0.1:<main_port>/api/approvals/stream/ws (server pushes a snapshot then patches of pending ApprovalInfo); POST /api/workspaces/summaries -> has_pending_approval
waiting_signals.meaning: A tool approval or an agent question is pending. Approvals live only in an in-memory DashMap (crates/services/src/services/approvals.rs), never on disk, and time out after 36000 s (utils/src/approvals.rs). The turn's execution_processes row stays 'running' the whole time, so waiting must override working. Rare in practice: every default profile in crates/executors/default_profiles.json skips permissions (Claude dangerously_skip_permissions, Codex danger-full-access, Amp dangerously_allow_all, Gemini and Qwen yolo, OpenCode auto_approve, Cursor force, Copilot allow_all_tools, Droid skip-permissions-unsafe), so a wait only happens for a profile variant with approvals or plan mode on. Port: $TMPDIR/vibe-kanban/vibe-kanban.port ({"main_port":N,"preview_proxy_port":M}) written by the browser-mode server only; the desktop app does not write it, so read its listening port with lsof. Origin header is checked only when present, no token. Unobserved.

hooks.config: None for the user. Only per-repository scripts, stored in db.v2.sqlite `repos` and edited in Settings -> Repositories: setup_script (once when the workspace starts), cleanup_script (after each coding-agent turn, run as an execution process with run_reason 'cleanupscript'), archive_script, dev_server_script. Each runs as `$SHELL -c <script>` (crates/executors/src/actions/script.rs). Notifications (sound, push) are toggles in config.json. VK itself injects a Claude Code Stop and PreToolUse hook callback over the SDK control channel to implement commit reminders and approvals (executors/src/executors/claude/client.rs); that is internal and not configurable.

telemetry.how: The local app sends Sentry errors and PostHog analytics only (crates/utils/src/sentry.rs; POSTHOG_API_KEY and POSTHOG_API_ENDPOINT are build-time and empty in source builds). OpenTelemetry exists only in the cloud `remote` server crate, exported to Azure Application Insights when APPLICATIONINSIGHTS_CONNECTION_STRING is set (crates/remote/src/lib.rs init_otel_layer); that service is being wound down. The agents VK launches may emit their own OTel if their env is set through a profile's `env` override (CmdOverrides.env), untested.

notes: Never seen running: every process shape below is read from source. VK is an orchestrator, not an agent: it spawns a fresh agent per turn (claude, codex, amp, gemini, copilot, qwen, opencode via npx; cursor-agent; droid) as a direct child of ITS server, and reads each agent's structured stdout. Consequences for a detector: (1) The registry should report the server or app as ONE host and never map its pid to a transcript. (2) The children it spawns can also match other rows (a native `claude` leaf under the npx cache, `cursor-agent`, `droid`), so drop a match whose ancestor is a Vibe Kanban host (README section 3 case 15), or the same work is counted twice as an idle Claude Code. (3) Exact per-workspace turn state is the SQLite or HTTP read described in working_signals, which the probe cannot do; until then only a weak file-mtime raise and tree CPU are left, and dev servers started from VK make both noisy. (4) To map a child to its workspace: the child's cwd is <worktree base>/<workspace dir>/<repo>, equal to workspaces.container_ref plus the repo name, and its environment has VK_WORKSPACE_ID (environment is not readable from the command line, so cwd is the practical key). (4b) A short-lived `osascript` or `afplay` child appears both when approval is needed and when a turn finishes (container.rs finalize_task sends 'Workspace Complete'), and only when notifications are on, so it is NOT a waiting signal and has been removed from waiting_signals. Exact waiting is the approvals WebSocket or has_pending_approval. (4c) A match on `vibe-kanban` by executable name is exact on argv[0] basename; a dev build (`cargo run`, binary `server`) is not matched. (5) The `npx vibe-kanban` node launcher, `vibe-kanban-mcp` (agents launch it over stdio, default `--mode global`) and `vibe-kanban-review` are not sessions and are not matched. The project is sunsetting (2026-04-10); the last npm release is 0.1.44 and main moved on to 0.1.45, so expect few new versions.
